title: The Mice in Council
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 老鼠们商量给猫挂铃铛，却没有一只敢去动手。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: SOME little Mice, who lived in the walls of a house, met together one night, to talk of the wicked Cat and to consider what could be done to get rid of her. The head Mice were Brown-back, Gray-ear, and White-whisker.
paragraphs.zh: 一些住在房屋墙洞里的小老鼠，一天夜里聚在一起，商量怎样对付那只可恶的猫，想找出摆脱她的办法。鼠群的首领是棕背、灰耳和白须。

paragraphs.en: “There is no comfort in the house,” said Brown-back. “If I but step into the pantry to pick up a few crumbs, down comes the Cat, and I have hardly time to run to my nest again.”
paragraphs.zh: “这屋里没有一点安宁，”棕背说，“我只要溜进食品柜捡几粒面包屑，猫就扑下来，我几乎来不及逃回洞里。”

paragraphs.en: “What can we do?” asked Gray-ear. “Shall we all run at her at once and bite her, and frighten her away?”
paragraphs.zh: “我们该怎么办？”灰耳问，“要不要大家一起冲上去咬她，把她吓跑？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” said White-whisker; “she is so bold we could not frighten her. I have thought of something better than that. Let us hang a bell round her neck. Then, if she moves, the bell will ring, and we shall hear it, and have time to run away.”
paragraphs.zh: “不行，”白须说，“她胆子那么大，我们吓不跑她。我有个更好的主意。我们给她脖子上挂个铃铛。这样，她一动铃铛就响，我们听见了，就有时间逃走。”

paragraphs.en: “O yes! yes!” cried all the Mice. “That is a capital idea. We will bell the Cat! Hurrah! hurrah! No more fear of the Cat!” and they danced in glee.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，对！对！”所有老鼠都叫起来，“这主意太妙了！我们给猫挂铃铛！万岁！万岁！再也不用怕猫了！”他们高兴得跳起舞来。

paragraphs.en: When their glee had subsided a little, Brown-back asked, “But who will hang the bell round her neck?”
paragraphs.zh: 等兴奋稍稍平息，棕背问：“可是，谁去把铃铛挂到她脖子上呢？”

paragraphs.en: No one answered. “Will you?” he asked of White-whisker.
paragraphs.zh: 没有一只老鼠回答。“你去吗？”他问白须。

paragraphs.en: “I don’t think I can,” replied White-whisker; “I am lame, you know. It needs some one who can move quickly.”
paragraphs.zh: “我看我不行，”白须回答，“你知道，我腿脚不方便。这活儿得找个动作快的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Excuse me,” answered Gray-ear; “I have not been well since that time when I was almost caught in the trap.”
paragraphs.zh: “恕难从命，”灰耳回答，“自从那次我差点被夹住，身体就一直不大好。”

paragraphs.en: “Who will bell the Cat, then?” said Brown-back. “If it is to be done, some one must do it.”
paragraphs.zh: “那么谁去给猫挂铃铛呢？”棕背说，“这事要办，总得有人去办啊。”

paragraphs.en: Not a sound was heard, and one by one the little Mice stole away to their holes, no better off than they were before.
paragraphs.zh: 一点声音也没有。小老鼠们一个接一个悄悄溜回洞里，处境和之前一样，毫无改善。

paragraphs.en: When there is trouble there is need of some one to act, as well as some one to advise.
paragraphs.zh: 遇到麻烦时，既需要有人出主意，也需要有人去行动。
